result.summary: Updates 1P1C package construction in TxDownloadManagerImpl to check if candidate orphan transactions are already in the mempool. If a candidate child exists in the mempool, it is erased from the orphanage and skipped. This preserves the invariant that package evaluation never receives an already-admitted child, retaining the Assume(false) assertion for MEMPOOL_ENTRY in net_processing.
result.problem: Orphan transactions that enter the mempool through non-peer mechanisms such as RPC submission are not automatically evicted from the orphanage. When a reconsiderable parent subsequently arrives from a peer, Find1P1CPackage could select that orphan as a package child, resulting in a MEMPOOL_ENTRY acceptance result that triggers an Assume(false) assertion failure in debug builds.
evidence: PR description: 'An orphan that enters the mempool other than through peer relay (e.g. by RPC) stays in the orphanage, so Find1P1CPackage can pick it as the child of a reconsiderable parent, and package evaluation then reports it as MEMPOOL_ENTRY, which hits Assume(false).'

The added functional test (test_orphan_in_mempool) reproduces the exact issue: an orphan submitted via submitpackage enters the mempool while remaining in the orphanage, triggering the code path upon receiving the reconsiderable parent.
result.changed_since_previous: Rather than removing the Assume(false) assertion in ProcessPackageResult and handling MEMPOOL_ENTRY as an acceptance notification, the PR now intercepts the case inside Find1P1CPackage, erasing the child from the orphanage and skipping it to keep the assertion intact.
result.card: This PR fixes a debug assertion failure during 1P1C package relay when an orphan child is already present in the mempool. Transactions entering the mempool through RPC or other non-peer paths are not pruned from the orphanage, previously allowing Find1P1CPackage to pick them as children for reconsiderable parents and triggering an Assume(false) on MEMPOOL_ENTRY during package evaluation. The change inspects candidate orphans in Find1P1CPackage, erasing them from the orphanage and skipping them if they are already in the mempool. A functional test is added to reproduce and verify the fix.

risk.why: A flaw in mempool existence checks or orphan erasure could prematurely discard valid orphan transactions or cause 1P1C package construction to fail during peer transaction relay.
